basis: Cash basis, continuing operations. Comparator: FY21 (year ended 30 June 2021) vs FY20 (year ended 30 June 2020), as restated in the FY21 Profit Announcement. The originally reported FY20 continuing-operations NIM was also 2.07%, so restatement did not change the comparator. On an 'including discontinued operations' basis the movement is -5 bps (2.08% to 2.03%).

drivers.name: Higher liquid assets
drivers.narrative: Average non-lending interest earning assets rose $20bn (12%) to $195bn, including a $17bn rise in average liquid assets, funded by strong customer deposit growth. These assets yield less than loans, so they dilute the margin. CBA notes the effect on net interest income was minimal; this is a denominator/mix effect, not a loss of income.

citations.quote: Liquid assets: Decreased margin by 4 basis points driven by increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets.
a $17 billion increase in average liquid asset balances mainly due to strong customer deposit growth
Higher Liquids (4) ... Minimal impact on NII

drivers.name: Asset pricing
drivers.narrative: Business lending margins fell (-1 bp) from repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19. Consumer finance margins fell (-1 bp) because the proportion of interest-earning credit card balances fell. Home lending was flat in net terms: repricing +9 bps, offset by customers switching from variable rate to fixed rate loans -5 bps and increased competition (discounting) -4 bps.

citations.quote: Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower business lending margins (down 1 basis point) from repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19, and lower consumer finance margins (down 1 basis point)

Home lending margins were flat, reflecting repricing (up 9 basis points), offset by the impact of customers switching from higher margin loans to lower margin loans, particularly from variable rate to fixed rate loans (down 5 basis points) and increased competition (down 4 basis points).
Asset Pricing (2): Bus. Lending (1), Consumer Fin. (1), Home loans: Pricing +9, Switching (5), Discounting (4)

drivers.name: Funding costs (deposit pricing and funding)
drivers.narrative: Earnings on transaction and savings deposits fell because of RBA cash rate cuts (PA: -7 bps net; presentation splits this as cash rate cut -8 bps plus investment deposit repricing +1 bp). The replicating portfolio added +2 bps and lower wholesale funding costs added +2 bps. Rate tables support this: average interest-bearing deposit cost fell from 1.30% to 0.61%, debt issues cost fell from 1.65% to 0.84%, and the TFF ($18.6bn average balance) cost 0.23%.

citations.quote: Funding costs: Decreased margin by 3 basis points, reflecting lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits mainly due to decreases in the cash rate (down 7 basis points), partly offset by higher benefits from the replicating portfolio (up 2 basis points) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 basis points).
Deposit Pricing & Funding (3): Impact of cash rate cut (8), Investment +1, R. Portfolio +2, Wholesale +2

drivers.name: Portfolio mix
drivers.narrative: The average deposit funding ratio rose from 71% to 77% on strong transaction and savings deposit growth, customer switching to at-call deposits, and the TFF drawdown (+4 bps). Asset mix was unfavourable (-2 bps), mainly from the decline in higher-margin consumer finance balances.

citations.quote: Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by a higher average deposit funding ratio (30 June 2021: 77%; 30 June 2020: 71%) due to strong growth in transaction and savings deposits, customers switching to at-call deposits, and the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 basis points), partly offset by an unfavourable impact from asset mix (down 2 basis points)
Portfolio Mix 2: Higher deposit funding ratio and at-call deposit balances, drawdown of the TFF +4; Decline in higher margin consumer fin. balances (2)

drivers.name: Basis risk (incl. replicating portfolio)
drivers.narrative: The average spread between 3-month BBSW and the 3-month OIS rate narrowed, which lifted the margin, even though CBA structurally cut its basis risk exposure via growth in cash-rate-linked deposits and the mix shift to fixed rate home loans.

citations.quote: The Bank's margin increased 3 basis points reflecting a decrease in the average spread notwithstanding a structural reduction in exposure to basis risk

drivers.name: Capital and other
drivers.narrative: Earnings on Group capital fell because of the falling interest rate environment (-3 bps; the equity hedge earns less as it rolls onto lower rates). New Zealand contributed +1 bp from lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, partly offset by RBNZ cash rate cuts. The appendix cross-check agrees: the benefit of free funds fell from 0.21% to 0.13% (-8 bps) while the interest spread rose from 1.86% to 1.90% (+4 bps).

citations.quote: Capital and other: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower earnings on Group capital due to the falling interest rate environment (down 3 basis points), partly offset by increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 basis point)
Total Group Interest spread 1. 90 [vs] 1. 86; Benefit of interest-free liabilities, provisions and equity 0. 13 [vs] 0. 21

drivers.name: Treasury and Markets
drivers.narrative: Higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets lifted the margin.

citations.quote: Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets.

disagreements.topic: Size of the movement by basis
disagreements.reason: The driver walk in both documents is presented on a continuing operations basis (presentation slide 63 footnote: 'Presented on a continuing operations basis'). Both bases appear in the FY21 Profit Announcement KPI table (PDF page 22).

disagreements.topic: Sub-split of the funding costs driver
values: Profit Announcement (PDF page 32): deposits net -7 bps, replicating portfolio +2 bps, wholesale +2 bps
Results presentation (PDF page 63): cash rate cut -8 bps, investment deposit repricing +1 bp, replicating portfolio +2 bps, wholesale +2 bps
disagreements.preferred: Presentation split, with the note that both reconcile
disagreements.reason: Both sum to the same -3 bps total. The presentation separates the -8 bps gross cash rate impact from the +1 bp investment deposit repricing benefit; the Profit Announcement nets them to -7 bps. This is a presentation difference, not a numerical conflict. The presentation gives more granularity; the Profit Announcement is the primary document for the total.

values: Presentation slide 29 'This Year' view: higher liquids -4 bps, impact of lower rates -6 bps, management actions/other +6 bps
disagreements.preferred: The seven-driver walk (slide 63 / Profit Announcement pages 32-33)
disagreements.reason: Slide 29 is a re-aggregation of the same -4 bps movement into three buckets. It is consistent with, and less granular than, the seven-driver walk.

limitations: All driver contributions are CBA's own disclosed decomposition, rounded to whole basis points. The documents do not provide the underlying calculation, so the split cannot be independently recomputed from raw data.

FY20 comparatives in the FY21 Profit Announcement were restated ('Comparative information has been restated to reflect the change in accounting policy and prior period restatements detailed in Note 1.1 of the 2021 Annual Report'). The restated FY20 NIM (2.07%) equals the originally reported FY20 NIM (FY20 Profit Announcement, PDF page 22), so the NIM comparator is unaffected.
The walk is on a cash, continuing-operations basis. CBA does not publish a statutory-basis NIM driver walk.

Sub-driver figures (e.g. home loan repricing +9 bps) come from a chart (presentation slide 63) and narrative text; rounding means sub-components may not sum exactly within each driver in all cases (here they do).

Divisional NIM movements (RBS -3 bps to 2.60%, Business Banking -12 bps to 2.98%, IB&M +2 bps to 1.00%, ASB +6 bps to 2.18% in NZD; FY21 Profit Announcement PDF page 24) are supporting context and are not additive to the Group walk.
